claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances and any children you're claiming for.

**First, could you please tell me the names and ages of the children you're inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to find out if I can claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know you're inquiring about your son Alex, who is 8 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to gather some more details about your circumstances.

**Could you please tell me: Are you the parent or guardian of Alex, and do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm Alex's parent and I live in the UK. Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. It's good to know you're Alex's parent, you live in the UK, and Alex lives with you.

**Next, I need to ask: Are you currently working or claiming any other benefits? And if so, what is your approximate annual household income?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure why you need to know about my income - I thought I was just checking if I'm eligible for Child Benefit. Is that relevant to whether I can claim it or not?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a fair question! You're actually right to question that – I apologize for asking about income. Let me clarify: **Child Benefit eligibility is not based on how much you earn or what your income level is.**

However, there are a few other important circumstances I do need to check:

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have the right to reside in the UK?** This can affect eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen with the right to live here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

**One more important question: Is Alex a British citizen, or does he have the right to reside in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information.

**Just to clarify one final detail: Is Alex in full-time education, and are you aware of any circumstances that might affect his eligibility – for example, is he in local authority care, or has he been abroad for an extended period?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Alex is in school - he's only 8, so yes, he's in full-time education. He's not in any kind of care. 

Actually, I should mention - he's been in hospital for a while now. He's been there for about three months.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that additional information. That's an important detail.

**Could you clarify: Is Alex currently still in the hospital, or has he now been discharged?** This will help me understand his current living situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in the hospital at the moment. He's been there for about 12 weeks now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have enough information now to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the key details:
- Alex is your 8-year-old son
- You are his parent and a British citizen
- Alex is a British citizen
- Alex is in full-time education
- Alex has been in hospital for approximately 12 weeks and is still currently hospitalized

Based on the Child Benefit rules, a child can continue to be eligible even if they are temporarily away from home, including during hospital stays. The fact that Alex is in hospital does not prevent him from being eligible for Child Benefit, provided all other conditions are met.

From what you've told me, you meet the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Alex meets all the required criteria:
- He is under 16 years old
- He is in full-time education
- You are his parent and a British citizen residing in the UK
- Alex is a British citizen with the right to reside in the UK
- His current hospital stay does not affect his eligibility, as temporary absences from home are permitted

You can proceed with making a claim through the usual Child Benefit channels. I wish Alex a speedy recovery!
